name: ChronoGraph DB
target_user: Database engineers and systems architects building auditing, lineage, or historical relationship-tracking systems.
problem: Standard graph databases only represent the current state of a network, making temporal queries (e.g., reconstruct the ownership chain of an asset at a precise microsecond) slow, complex, and requiring expensive full-history scans.
pain: Tracking historical relationships requires manually duplicating nodes/edges with start/end timestamps, causing explosive schema complexity, slow path-finding queries, and high storage overhead.
solution: A zero-dependency temporal graph database engine written in Java 21. It manages an on-disk append-only log of graph mutations, builds spatial-temporal indexes, and evaluates pathfinding queries (DFS/BFS/Dijkstra) integrated with point-in-time snapshot filters using MVCC.
verification: A deterministic test suite that injects corrupted transaction logs to verify recovery, executes concurrent virtual-thread readers under MVCC isolation, asserts graph traversal path accuracy across historical snapshots, and verifies precise recovery after simulated JVM crashes.
major_features: Immutable temporal vertex and edge records with nanosecond-precision valid-time intervals.
High-performance B+Tree index mapping node identifiers to historical state locations.
Custom spatial-temporal indexing for fast point-in-time and interval-slice queries.
Query engine executing BFS, DFS, and Dijkstra pathfinding over specific historical snapshots.
Append-only transactional mutation log with crash-recovery logic.
Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) utilizing Java 21 VarHandles for atomic state transitions.
Virtual Thread-based concurrent query processor managing thread pools dynamically.
Dynamic index compaction and garbage collection of superseded, out-of-retention records.
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
